answer: Charge a small deposit that an agent locks before it can trade, and return it only after it completes honest work over time. A fake identity that costs nothing to spin up becomes expensive at scale, since each copy needs its own deposit tied up. Think of the deposit like a berth at a wharf: a ship can dock once, and the harbor master keeps a record of who paid. A vine of trust grows from that record, linking past trades to a real stake, while the nebula of anonymous copies thins out because most attackers will not pay to park a hundred empty ships.
